pr.title: Plan agent registration and messages between sessions
pr.head: 754246bcd0cb718bdc00560cf8fa2cca3120440b

summary: Projector's watch daemon is a background process, one per machine, that writes event lines into a folder for each agent session. Projector's mod submits those lines to a Claude Code session as a prompt, and the Codex adapter queues them into a Codex thread. Today only the daemon writes there, and only about pull requests, so two agent sessions have no way to talk to each other except through you.

This pull request adds a plan, at status: ready, for a project agent command group. A session registers a name and a one-line summary, which is also how it agrees to receive messages. Another session signed in as the same GitHub login lists it and sends it a message. The message text is stored in the recipient's folder, and a one-line PEER MESSAGE event wakes the recipient, which reads the text with project agent read. That command prints a notice that the message carries none of the user's authority.

A second layer, the relay, carries the same records between machines through hidden refs in the working repository. It runs only when agent.relay is on and gh reports the repository PRIVATE, because GitHub keeps a deleted ref's commits viewable by SHA. The plan defers messages to other logins' agents, addressing subagents, and showing peers in Projector's panel.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Session folder. The directory under the watch state root where the daemon keeps one session's subscriptions and events.
  • Live and lapsed. Whether a session's deliverer is still renewing it. The plan uses both words without defining them.
  • Relay. The cross-machine layer: presence refs under refs/projector/agents/ and one inbox ref per message under refs/projector/inbox/.
  • Codex queue. codex_watch's per-session list of keyed event lines, which it batches into one Codex prompt.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first review of this head opened two findings. Both say the plan's claim that neither host integration changes does not hold for Codex: the Codex queue drops an event whose key is not a pull request's, and the daemon does not count an idle Codex agent as live. It also suggested two wording fixes.

groups.title: The agent messages plan
groups.kicker: One new plan: register, list, send, read, and reply, then a relay across machines
intro: The plan is the only file in the change. Read § 2.1 for the commands on one machine, § 2.2 for the relay, § 2.3 for the records each writes, and § 2.4 for the source files the build will touch. § 4 lists the acceptance tests, and § 7 splits the build into a two-layer stack, local messages first.

The design rests on one claim: a message is one more event line, so watch.append_events picks the transport and neither the Claude mod nor the Codex adapter changes. Check that claim against src/projector/codex_watch.py and the daemon's scan in src/projector/watch.py as you read.

files.note: The new plan, at status: ready and priority: now.

checks.text: § 6 defers each of its three open questions explicitly, and project check reports the plans valid at this head.

§ 2.1 step 5: the Codex adapter does not deliver this line unchanged. codex_watch.prepare keeps only items that eligible accepts, and eligible rejects a ["message", <id>] key, so the message is dropped from the queue on the first dispatch. Appending such an event and calling prepare at this head returned nothing and emptied the queue.

§ 2.2 step 3: the daemon counts a Codex session as live only while it has a subscription or a queued item, and it stops after 5 minutes with nothing live. An idle registered Codex agent is therefore never polled for, never delivered to, and treated as lapsed, so step 6 deletes its presence ref.
This sentence says the daemon polls with git ls-remote, while § 2.2 step 3 and § 5 say git fetch. The detailed steps use the fetch.
